parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile federal layer (binary sex definition, no X markers, visa adjudication instructed to refuse on sex doubt with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, federal single-sex facility ban, immigration-custody abuse reports) with a state enforcing birth-sex restroom rules since 4 Dec 2025, ID checks within days, a documented arrest with 24h in a men's ward, marker-change bans, and a July 2026 top-tier 'Do Not Travel' grade. Mitigating: no identity criminalisation, functioning courts enjoining orders, federal hate-crime and employment protections, legal aid. Recorded killings are near background, not organised targeting. Net: Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal Feb-2025 cable instructs refusal where document discrepancy casts reasonable doubt on sex, plus possible permanent fraud ineligibility; X markers halted; travellers report passports blocked or confiscated, some stranded; multiple foreign advisories issued.
entry_documents.protection: Findings require all four fraud elements, are never automatic, limited waivers exist; litigation pending; existing X passports valid to expiry.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal can cascade into onward-travel loss and, if documents are questioned as deceptive, state facility rules keyed to birth-certificate sex compound mismatch exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans woman arrested 19 Mar 2025 charged with trespass, held 24 hours in the men's ward; federal immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans men; federal corrections adoption of hormone-withdrawal policies.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Trespass offence requires willful entry plus refusal to leave, not automatic arrest; pretrial release granted; courts deny immunity defences in part; no cell-assignment rule in state gender-placement statute.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor stopped under the state facility law or held federally can be placed by birth sex, and complaint-making carries documented retaliation risk in custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State law (effective 4 Dec 2025) requires restrooms matching birth-certificate sex across schools, universities, prisons and state buildings with $25k/$125k fines; federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; ID checks at capitol restrooms began within days; DOJ escalated a school-district enforcement inquiry Apr 2026.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states, 4 units and the capital district have no such ban; capital city council and opponents contest enforcement; only 4 states criminalise access and only via trespass.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal funding and DOJ enforcement amplify state bans, so a visitor entering airports, federal buildings, campuses or state sites carries continuous mismatch exposure.

care_services.exposure: State has banned gender-affirming care for minors since June 2023; federal orders and proposed insurance rules target youth care; crisis-lifeline LGBTQ services shut nationally; DOJ subpoenaed hospital records of under-19s.
care_services.protection: Adult care is not documented as banned; national employment ruling recognised by state courts; legal-aid FAQ maintains documentation guidance; some orders enjoined.
care_services.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a parent faces statewide care prohibition plus federal investigation posture toward adults facilitating transition.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; justice-department guidance uses 'radical gender ideology'; state definition act and Jan-2025 directive recognise only two genders; 66% poll support for birth-sex markers; DOJ tip-line driven enforcement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward criteria never list gender ideology as a trigger; strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; documented pushback from city officials and civil-rights lawyers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the probability that routine contact becomes an identity check, converting street-level friction into state-conducted outing.

minors_guardians.exposure: State parental-rights and school statutes mandate misgendering and ban LGBT student groups; federal order directs criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition; care ban applies to any visiting minor; facility law reaches public schools a visiting minor may enter.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented visitor-facing custody or guardianship penalty; injunctions have blocked investigation directives; adoption regardless of orientation permitted.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans parent travelling with a minor can be drawn into investigation framing only through school or care contacts, not automatically at entry.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 44 recorded killings of trans women 2008-2025 (about 7.6 per 100k trans women yearly); state hate-crime statute excludes gender identity and prosecutions are rare; no statewide nondiscrimination law; city LGBTQ ordinance rescinded Dec 2025.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; several cities bar discrimination; recorded rate sits near the general national homicide baseline, indicating background rather than organised targeting.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of state-level recourse means an assaulted visitor relies on federal charging and local police willingness, both uneven.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Guidance on the facilities law is unclear with warned uneven enforcement; DOJ school inquiry outcome unsourced; renewability of existing changed markers after Sept 2025 unsourced; 'Do Not Travel' tier has no later update.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined several federal orders; ACLU suit pending; running legal-aid FAQ; functioning judiciary issued merits rulings for trans plaintiffs.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Live litigation means exposure fluctuates by travel date, but remedies operate slowly relative to a short visit.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A: Vellandra imposes universal entry exclusion with no remedy, whereas here refusal is discretionary, requires four fraud elements, and is contested in court; imprisonment for identity itself is not on the books. Similarity lies in documented, consistent identity-based entry friction affecting a class of travellers.

Closest match. 0.45-A features routine checkpoint exposure, documented detention and denial of care, uncommon prosecutions, scarce legal aid and inconsistent enforcement. This dossier adds an actual arrest with birth-sex ward placement and an official Do-Not-Travel grade, but also stronger federal protections and active judicial review.

Higher than 0.55-B: Kestrel Isles offers administrative secondary screening and refusal only, with written reasons and appeal. Here exposure extends to arrest, birth-sex custody, enforced facility exclusion and federal custody abuse reports, not merely delayed entry.

Well above 0.75-C, which pairs trained officers, tribunal appeals and compensation for brief detention. This jurisdiction documents hostile statutes, active enforcement and custody mistreatment, so the functioning-remedy similarity cannot lift it into Reduced Risk.

parsed.synthesis: Two sovereign layers reinforce rather than offset each other: federal document and facility policy plus a state enforcing birth-sex restroom rules with documented ID checks, a trespass arrest and 24 hours in a men's ward. Universal exposures — entry screening keyed to sex doubt, airport and government-building facility exclusion, birth-sex placement if detained — follow every outed visitor regardless of itinerary, and a trans minor additionally faces a statewide care ban. Violence sits near background homicide, not organised targeting, and no identity criminalisation exists. Functioning courts, federal hate-crime coverage, city protections and pending litigation prevent a lower band, but unremedied documented exposures keep the rating in Elevated Risk rather than Reduced Risk.
